newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG signs palm oil deal with Kulim.
newsitem.headline: PNG signs palm oil deal with Kulim.

text.p: The Papua New Guinea government on Friday signed a deal for the sale of a palm oil project on New Britain island to Malaysia's Kulim Bhd for 154 million kina (US$115 million).

PNG Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance Chris Haiveta signed the deal transferring ownership of the New Britain Oil Palm project to the Malaysian firm and hailed it as a sign of the return of investor confidence in the country.

The Malaysian company will own 90 percent of the palm oil project, which has been in operation for over a decade, while the PNG government retains the other 10 percent, which will be held in trust for landowners and the host provincial government.
"I am very pleased with the outcome of the negotiations and finalisation of the deal, especially with the absence of a stock exchange," Haiveta said.
"It shows a most welcome new interest by foreign investors in the agro-industrial potential of Papua New Guinea," he added.

Haiveta said the government was also pleased with agreements reached with the new owners, including the return of up to 20 percent of the shares now held by Kulin to the PNG public through a planned float within five years.
Of the 90 percent share sold to Kulim, the government will also buy back 20 percent on a "carried" basis, Haiveta said.
He said that would be paid back from the government's earning from its shareholding.
The New Britain Oil Palm was previously owned jointly by Britain's Harrisons & Crosfield Plc and the government.
The government earlier this year bought Harrisons & Crosfield's 54 percent stake for over $65 million and has now sold on those shares to Kulim.
